chunks: Sa'd, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Rāzī, who said:

I was with some companions of mine on a journey, and I was their Imam. So I led them in the Maghrib salat, then I gave salām after the first two rakʿahs. My companions said: “You only led us in two rakʿahs.” So I spoke to them and they spoke to me. Then they said: “As for us, we will repeat.” I said: “But I will not repeat; rather, I will complete it with one rakʿah.” So I completed it with one rakʿah. Then we departed, and I came to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and mentioned to him what had happened with us. He said to me: “You were more correct than them in action. Only the one who does not know what he prayed repeats.”

So he عليه السلام clarified in this report that whoever does not know what he prayed must repeat, according to what we have stated before, while in the first two hadiths there is that which prevents reliance upon them, namely the hadith of Dhū al-Shimālayn and the forgetfulness of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and this is among that which intellects reject. As for what is contained in the other hadith, which we made a supporting witness for the first two hadiths, from his statement, “So I spoke to them and they spoke to me,” it does not contradict what we mention: that whoever speaks intentionally in the salat, repeating the salat becomes obligatory upon him, for two reasons.

One of them is that it is not stated in the report that he said, “I spoke to them and they spoke to me,” whether intentionally or forgetfully; and when that is not present in it, we interpret it as forgetfulness. The second is that even if there were an explicit statement of intention in it, it would still be possible that what is meant is one who gave salām in the salat forgetfully and assumed that this was a cause permitting speech, just as it is a cause permitting it after departing from the salat. So repeating the salat would not be obligatory upon him because of his ignorance of that and because his knowledge that this is not permissible had been absent. As for what he narrated:

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the first two units of prayer after which salām was given mistakenly
key_terms.السَّهْوِ: forgetfulness or inadvertent mistake in salat
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repeating the salat from the beginning
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib salat, which consists of three rakʿahs
key_terms.رَكْعَةٍ: a single rakʿah added to complete the prayer
key_terms.لَا يَدْرِي: not knowing or being uncertain about what one has prayed

ai.seo_question: When must a person repeat the salat after making a mistake or speaking during prayer?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a ruling on forgetfulness in salat, especially when one gives salām before completing Maghrib. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام affirms that completing the deficient salat is more correct than repeating it when the worshipper knows what he has prayed, while repetition applies to one who does not know what he performed. The accompanying discussion also explains how speaking during salat in such a case may be understood in light of forgetfulness or ignorance.
